title: Cross-surface variant mapping and prototyping library for budget forecast widgets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: The cost and forecast cards used across the Console (Projects Spend, Dedicated Capacity forecast, and Cost Rollout previews) have accumulated divergent visual variants and inconsistent token usage. This makes it difficult for PMs and engineers to assemble new dashboard surfaces quickly and creates maintenance debt when token updates are applied.

Goal: Create a cross-surface Figma library of interactive variants for budget/forecast widgets that documents mapping rules between design tokens, component states, and runtime props used by the Console rendering system. Deliver a prototype kit demonstrating canonical variants (compact, detailed, alerting, and rollout-preview) and clear token naming guidance to prevent future divergence.

Scope: Design tokens (spacing, type, color, elevation), card component variants with accessible state treatment, micro-interactions for thresholds (expand/collapse, alert banners), and a rollout-preview state that mirrors backend flags (canary vs main). Produce a Figma component library, a short handoff doc, and a small set of annotated examples for engineering integration (including JSON-like spec for runtime props).
acceptance_criteria: Figma library published with documented component variants: compact, standard, expanded, alerting, and rollout-preview
Token mapping table that ties each visual property (e.g., bg, border, text, accent) to the Console token name and intended runtime prop
Accessibility checklist applied: contrast ratios verified, keyboard focus states defined, and screen-reader labels included
Prototype includes 3 real-world dashboard instances (Projects Spend, Dedicated Forecast, Cost Rollout Preview) showing correct token application
Handoff doc with example runtime props (JSON-like) and two sample GitHub PR comments linking to components for engineering
Design sign-off from PM and two ENG reviewers recorded in comments
deliverables: Token mapping CSV attached to the handoff doc
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Initial kickoff completed with PM and ENG leads. Agreed to focus on three canonical surfaces first to limit scope and validate token mappings with real telemetry (top 10 projects). PM suggested rollout-preview should show both canary and fallback visuals.

2026-03-04 - Marco Chen: Prototype v0 in Figma uploaded. Highlights: compact vs expanded layouts, new token candidates for 'card-elevation-2' and 'accent-alert'. Need ENG input on whether 'accent-alert' maps to existing runtime flag or requires new prop. Linked draft handoff: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Budget+Widget+Variant+Mapping

2026-03-06 - Priya Singh (PM): Feedback - prefer using existing 'cost-danger' semantic token rather than creating 'accent-alert' to reduce infra churn. Also requested an explicit rollout-preview visual showing how metric regression triggers the alert state.

2026-03-08 - Marco Chen: Updated Figma with 'cost-danger' mapping and added annotated variant for rollout-preview. Ran preliminary contrast checks; all text sizes meet WCAG AA except small-caption on alert banners — proposed increasing font-size to 12px. Created ENG ticket for props: ENG-5021.

2026-03-10 - Josh Reynolds (Engineering reviewer): Reviewed prototype. Notes: liked the token mapping table. Two action items: 1) make sure the 'compact' variant supports KV cache tooltip (needs an inline icon slot), 2) provide JSON example for 'rollout_preview' prop with canary_percentage and fallback_behavior. Attached a suggested JSON in the PR comment (https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5823).
notes: Trade-offs: Keeping token surface minimal reduces runtime coupling but requires some visual compromises for highly dense displays. We decided to prefer semantic tokens (cost-success/cost-warning/cost-danger) over creating many specific accent tokens to make future theming easier. Engineering asked for a small, machine-readable props spec rather than a full component API rewrite.
open_questions: Should rollout-preview expose canary_percentage as an integer prop or as an envelope object to allow future metadata?
Do we standardize the compact card's action area (three-dot menu) across all dashboard surfaces, or allow contextual actions per view?
If we increase the caption font-size for a11y, do layout constraints require tightening token spacing (gap tokens) to keep card heights stable?
